name: Salamãy

Supporting: Hanke, Wanda. 1950. Breves notas sôbre os índios Mondé e o seu idioma. Dusenia (Curitiba) 1(4): 215-228, p. 217 (page image).
catalog_locator: Moore 2005 p. 519 (PDF p. 5), first paragraph; p. 515 (PDF p. 1), end of the Salamãy section; appendix symbol key p. 520 (PDF p. 6). Hanke 1950 p. 217 (archive.org scan PDF p. 5), 'VOCABULÁRIO MONDÉ' transcription note.
catalog_quote: Os sistemas tonais de Salamãy e Aruá ainda não têm uma análise sólida, fato que impede o uso dos fenômenos tonais como evidência para a classificação interna. Todavia, Os resultados preliminares apontam na mesma direção dos outros critérios: Salamãy e Suruí têm dois tons contrastivos e prolongamento contrastivo, sem contornos, enquanto os dialetos da língua A têm contornos. A existência de um passo descendente (downstep) foi confirmada em Gavião, Zoró e Cinta Larga e é provável em Aruá. Este fonômeno não existe em Surui e provavelmente também não em Salamãy. [p. 519] ... Os dados apresentados são de Maria Campés, colhidos em Porto Velho. O tom e o prolongamento vocálico ainda estão sendo estabelecidos. [p. 515] ... Suprassegmentais ilustrados com a vogal a: á tom alto ... aa vogal prolongada ... â tom subindo ... a.a duas sílabas ... a tom baixo ... ã vogal nasal [p. 520]. — Hanke 1950 p. 217: 'O acento circunflexo ^ significa uma pronúncia larga, o til ~ uma pronúncia nasal. A sílaba que leva o acento principal marco com o agudo ´. Vogais que se pronunciam à parte, escrevo separadamente, como p. ex., ha-ái.'

new_statements.translation: The tonal systems of Salamãy and Aruá do not yet have a solid analysis, which prevents the use of tonal phenomena as evidence for the internal classification. However, the preliminary results point in the same direction as the other criteria: Salamãy and Suruí have two contrastive tones and contrastive vowel length, without contours, whereas the dialects of language A have contours. The existence of a downstep was confirmed in Gavião, Zoró and Cinta Larga and is probable in Aruá. This phenomenon does not exist in Suruí and probably not in Salamãy either.
new_statements.citation: Moore, Denny. 2005. Classificação interna da família lingüística Mondé. Estudos Lingüísticos XXXIV: 515-520.
new_statements.locator: p. 519 (PDF p. 5), first paragraph; cf. p. 515 'O tom e o prolongamento vocálico ainda estão sendo estabelecidos.'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (6 pp., text layer, Estudos Linguisticos XXXIV 515-520). extracted text of PDF p. 5 (journal p. 519, first paragraph, immediately after the VVC:VCV correspondence table) gives the quoted passage character for character, including the oddities 'Todavia, Os', 'fonômeno' and 'Surui': 'Os sistemas tonais de Salamãy e Aruá ainda não têm uma análise sólida.. Salamãy e Suruí têm dois tons contrastivos e prolongamento contrastivo, sem contornos.. Este fonômeno não existe em Surui e provavelmente também não em Salamãy.' The p. 515 cross-reference is also verbatim: 'Os dados apresentados são de Maria Campés, colhidos em Porto Velho. O tom e o prolongamento vocálico ainda estão sendo estabeleci…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Salamãy is described as a tone language with two contrastive level tones (high marked by acute, low unmarked in Moore's appendix) plus contrastive vowel length and no contour tones; no word-stress rule is given anywhere. The only stress remark in the literature is Hanke 1950 p. 217, who marks 'the syllable bearing the main accent' with an acute in her wordlist without stating where it falls (most of her marked forms carry it on the final syllable, but that is my count of her list, not her statement).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Moore flags the Salamãy tonal analysis as preliminary (p. 515, p. 519); tone/length transcription in the appendix still being established.
new_statements.domain_note: Moore's data are isolated words (cognate wordlist) from one semi-speaker, Maria Campés, recorded in Porto Velho; Hanke's 1950 list is citation-form words and a few phrases from three families met on the upper Guaporé. Hanke 1950 p. 217 (saved PDF, page image verified): 'O acento circunflexo ^ significa uma pronúncia larga, o til ~ uma pronúncia nasal. A sílaba que leva o acento principal marco com o agudo ´.'
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog sala1273 'Salamãi' = ISO mnd 'Mondé' = Moore's 'Salamãy'; Moore 2005 p. 515 explains that 'Mondé' was the name of a chief, not the tribe, so Hanke 1950's 'índios Mondé' (three families met on the upper Guaporé, main village on the Rio Pimenta Bueno/Apediá) are the same language, although Loukotka 1968 lists 'Mondé' and 'Sanamaica/Salamay' as separate entries. Moore's data come from one semi-speaker (Maria Campés, Porto Velho), one of three semi-speakers alive in 2005; the language is dormant.

new_statements.quote: We will be mainly concerned with the languages and dialects of the Mondé family, all of which have contrastive tone and length. Of the Aruá (ISO: arx), who have been in contact since the 1930s, only five speak their language. There are two semi-speakers of Salamãy (also called Mondé, ISO: mnd), who have also been in contact since the 1930s. [...] The speech of four tribes of Group B, Aruá, Gavião, Zoró, and Cinta Larga, is mutually intelligible, but that of the Salamãy is significantly different from these, though closer to Group B than to Surui.
new_statements.citation: Moore, Denny and Meyer, Julien (2014). The Study of tone and related phenomena in an Amazonian tone language: Gavião of Rondônia. Language Documentation and Conservation. pp. 613–636.

There are two semi-speakers of Salamãy (also called Mondé, ISO: mnd), who have also been in contact since the 1930s.' and '.. but that of the Salamãy is significantly different from these, though closer to Group B than to Surui.' (the rea…
new_statements.relation_note: Same type as the existing statement (Moore 2005: Salamãy has two contrastive tones plus length, no stress statement). Moore & Meyer 2014 repeats the family-level claim of contrastive tone and length and adds nothing on stress for Salamãy; the catalog rule field stays empty. The work is primarily about Gavião (gvo), not Salamãy.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Salamãy is named only as a Mondé-branch language, and the Mondé branch is characterised wholesale as having contrastive tone and vowel length. Nothing is said about where word stress falls in Salamãy, whether stress exists, or whether it is contrastive. The paper's only stress discussion (pp. 615-616) concerns Surui and Gavião: a missionary's report that a Surui disyllable could be 'stressed on both syllables' is reinterpreted as high tone, and in a Gavião 'fat'/'egg' minimal pair 'consultants judged the word to be fat, giving importance to the tone and not the stress'.
new_statements.identity_note: The work's object language is Gavião of Rondônia (ISO gvo), with comparative Zoró and Surui data; Salamãy (ISO mnd, 'also called Mondé') is mentioned once as a Mondé-branch language with two semi-speakers, classified per Moore 2005 as closer to Group B (Aruá, Gavião, Zoró, Cinta Larga) than to Surui. No Salamãy forms are cited.

No placement rule is stated. In the ~300-word list the acute sits on the final syllable in most marked forms (papá, kokú, indú, barúm, umbaktí, apatzerá, tzurê..) with some non-final marks (umbák/umbak, ha-ái, chíwa); this is my observation from the list, not a statement by Hanke.
